So two of attempt 2's three majors (V depth, and the run-angle half of the attitude finding) are substantially fixed. The third (V too wide) regressed, the outer-edge half of the attitude finding regressed, and two locked features were dented. The correction pushed the notches outboard and the point down; the depth came right, the width overshot.

RECOMMENDATION: this is attempt 3 of 3. Every remaining fault is an attitude/proportion drift, not an identity fault - a customer comparing this against any other collar in the catalog would identify the faceted stepped leaf instantly, and the two features that most define the option (the step and the acute point) are correct and measured. If one more generation is available, spend it on ONE thing: move each notch apex outboard from 0.256 S to 0.286 S inboard of its own collar point, and pull the band corners in so the point-to-point spread is 2.1x the band width, while explicitly locking the sixteen items above. If no generation is available, this image is materially better than candidate-2 on six of eleven measured proportions and worse on four; I would keep candidate-3 as the best of the three but would not mark it verified.

MEASUREMENT PROVENANCE
Method: the drawing's geometry comes from intensity-weighted centroids of the red line-work (redness = R - (G+B)/2), subpixel. The render's geometry comes from the centreline of the edge-highlight ribbon isolated as (luminance minus a 15 px Gaussian) > 6, opened 3x3, three largest components - this reproduces a clean line drawing of the render that can be overlaid on the tech pack. Candidate-2 was re-measured with the identical pipeline before any 'better/worse' claim was made; it reproduces the previous QC's run angles (23.66/23.61 vs their 23.78/23.09) and the drawing's outer-edge segments (44.4/68 vs their 45/68.6), so the two pipelines agree and the deltas above are real, not method drift. Landmark validated first: tip-to-tip span S, present and unambiguous in both images; a second normalisation (the leaf's own frame, origin at the tip, axis tip->front point) gives notch position 0.320 along / 0.348 across in the render vs 0.323 / 0.379 in the drawing, so the notch findings survive both normalisations.

READINGS DISCARDED RATHER THAN REPORTED
1. A gradient ridge-tracker following the left leaf's outer edge jumped onto the shoulder/yoke seam at y~380 and was at x=0.9 by y=400 - the same trap the previous QC recorded. Discarded. The upper outer-edge segment was re-measured from the background silhouette (y 220-360, both sides) and the lower from the edge highlight (y 460-620), never crossing the seam.
2. On the drawing, a row-tracker seeded at x=150.5 for the right outer edge locked onto the neck-opening line (x 150 -> 127 descending) instead of the leaf edge. Discarded; replaced by a rightmost-red-per-row trace (x 150 -> 190).
3. The gradient ridge of the render's leaf edge follows the INNER boundary of the ~20 px edge-highlight band, not the leaf outline, and shifted the left apex by ~20 px. Discarded; all render geometry uses the ribbon centreline.
4. Locating the front point by intersecting the two arm fits gives y=845 in the render and y=162 in the drawing, against observed convergences of y~858 and y~169, because the arms curve inward near the bottom in BOTH images. All reported V figures use the observed convergence, not the intersection. My first pass at the drawing's right notch (155, 106.5) was 3 px off for the same reason and was replaced by a proper two-line intersection at (152.2, 105.6).
5. My own first coarse estimate of the drawing's outer-edge upper segment (50.4 deg, from binary-mask column centres over only 12 columns) was wrong; the subpixel trace over 17 rows gives 44.4 deg with sd 0.48 px. I used the subpixel figure.

COULD NOT MEASURE
- No centimetre figure is recoverable. The tech pack is a 226x226 line drawing with no printed dimension callout anywhere (1,919 red pixels, all line-work, zero digits or text). Every number above is a ratio.
- Collar stand height at the front: hidden behind the leaves in the drawing and by the viewing angle in the render.
- Stitch gauge / stitches per inch: the drawing carries no stitch callout, so the render's ~0.023 S edge-stitch inset is neither confirmed nor contradicted.
- The drawing's two collar-stand front edges converge at (112.5, 152), 0.11 S above and 0.026 S right of the leaf front point - a real asymmetry in the drawing. Only the left corresponding line is traceable in the render (the right is a shadow, not a highlight), so I could not give a number for it.
- The right band top corner in the render is a rounded junction; I could not place it to better than +/-6 px, which is +/-1.5% on the band-span ratio. The finding survives that uncertainty by a wide margin.

SPEC NOTES (unchanged from attempt 2, still worth fixing upstream): spec.json lists 'hexagon pocket' as a required shape token for a shirt collar - a text-extraction artefact; the drawing shows no pocket and the render correctly has none. spec.json also describes a 'band-style stand collar' while the drawing plainly shows a turndown collar with two pointed leaves; the drawing wins, and the render follows the drawing, which is correct.
